> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec7a5af47e83b0d57609e3231d1918f91df3eb19` — the merge of head `075fa174e61e43e962844e8ff2dd7fff75da39ef` into base `d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec7a5af47e83b0d57609e3231d1918f91df3eb19 && git checkout ec7a5af47e83b0d57609e3231d1918f91df3eb19
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83 075fa174e61e43e962844e8ff2dd7fff75da39ef && git checkout -B drift-repro d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83 && git merge --no-ff 075fa174e61e43e962844e8ff2dd7fff75da39ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d1f8ce8658b937d3685df62b04e2e478430b8e83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `075fa174e61e43e962844e8ff2dd7fff75da39ef`
Local-runs: none

Isolated reviewer, read at 2026-10-01T03:55Z. Inputs and nothing else: card #20995 (body and all four comments: triage `5923142248`, claim `5923572624`, dev report `5924254306`, seat ACCEPT `5924277913`), PR #21051 (body, five-file list, the net diff from merge base `2f2fa11d` to the head), and the head's check-runs. The seven commits `main` gained since the merge base touch none of the PR's five paths. ⚠️ Security card: everything below is stated by class and position only.

### Gate verdicts, read off the head's check-runs

Waited for the head's CI to finish before writing (two polls, three minutes apart). 35 check-runs on the head, all completed: 31 `success`, 4 `skipped` (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — path-filtered or opt-in, none a required context), 0 failed. All seven required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core (and its six shards), Dogfood Regression Gate (and its three shards), Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Also green: Check Changeset (the PR Automation job that carries the ADR-0087 registration gate and the no-major guard), the claim guards, Spec property liveness, the four Type Check leaves and Dogfood Verify CLI. These conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing was built, run or re-run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, with the verdict on it.

1. **One derivation — right.** `resolveCallerPosture` is read at exactly two sites: the engine middleware (its `secMeta`, which every gate downstream reads: the capability AND-gate, the CRUD gate, the FLS write gate, the masked-echo refusal 2.5a, the aggregate-input guard 2.5b, the predicate guard 2.9 and the step-4 result masker) and `resolveProjectionFieldMask`, which all three published projections (`getReadableFields` / `getMetadataReadableFields`, `getWritableFields`, `getQueryableFields`) go through. For a caller with one or more sets it returns the real posture, so that class is byte-identical to before. For a caller with none it returns the stand-in with two things carried from the posture: the masking-rule map and the resolved flag. `computePartialMaskRules` is untouched and has no empty-set short-circuit (an empty capability set lifts no rule), so the stand-in's rule map is what turns every reader from "stored and queryable" to "masked and not queryable" at once. No second reading of masking is introduced; only the input to the one reading changed. The one reader of masking outside this derivation is the explain engine's injected dep, which reads the posture directly: it agrees with the stand-in on masking by construction (same rule map) and disagrees only on the capability fold for this class, which is the pre-existing F3 the dev reported, not a change this diff makes.

2. **Served value for the class: stored → masked — right.** Step 4 was never gated on a resolved set; it was inert for the class because the old stand-in carried an empty rule map. The read partial-mask rules for an empty set are every declared rule (the explicit-deny subtraction has nothing to subtract from an empty evaluator map). Pinned three ways in the unit suite, each case asserting the zero-set premise first, and on two real-boot doors in the dogfood pin.

3. **Query accept set for the class: filter, sort, group and aggregate naming a masked field → refused 403 — right.** Step 2.9 was never gated on a set; 2.5b was and is now ungated. Both read `computeQueryGuardFieldPerms`, whose map for the class is exactly its masked fields (the evaluator's map for no sets is empty, the capability fold is deliberately not carried). The unit suite proves the published `getQueryableFields` equal to the two guards' verdicts field for field across the four query positions.

4. **Write accept set for the class: an echoed mask → refused 400 — right, and necessary.** Ungating 2.5a is the one edit beside the claim's named regions in the same file, and it is load-bearing: a caller now served the mask would otherwise save it back over the stored value. The dev declared it; the seat accepted it; I judge it part of the fix, not scope creep. Callers with sets are unaffected (their condition already held).

5. **`getQueryableFields` for the class: full set → full set minus masked — right.** This is the one published answer that moves, and its contract (a subset of the read projection differing by exactly the fields the caller is served masked) now holds for this class as it did for every other.

6. **`getReadableFields` / `getWritableFields` / `getMetadataReadableFields` for the class — unchanged on a resolved posture, as claimed.** The evaluator's field map for no sets is empty, the stand-in's capability contract is empty, so nothing is non-readable or non-editable and a masked field is kept as a served column: the full set, which is what the service contract in `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` states for the data plane. ⚠️ One branch is narrower than the PR body's "answer as before": on an unreadable posture these now answer `[]` for the class where they answered the full set before. That is the same fail-closed tier every other caller already got, the changeset declares it ("one more refusal"), and the field-universe resolver and the posture resolver read the same two sources in the same order, so it is reached only where the universe resolves and the posture does not — a corner, on the safe side. Judged right; the PR body's sentence is right on every resolved posture.

7. **Middleware fail-closed on an unreadable posture now reaches the class — right.** The rules come from that posture; while it is unreadable they are unknown. Declared in the changeset. Principal-less and system contexts still short-circuit before it.

8. **The principal-less boundary — preserved, one predicate.** `isPrincipalLessContext` is the old middleware condition extracted byte-for-byte (no position, no named set, no user id) and is now read by the middleware hand-off and by the projection's early answer, so an absent or empty context still answers the full set and is still handed through. A context naming only sets that resolve to nothing, or holding only an audience anchor no set is named after, carries a principal and reaches the gates. The unit suite pins both sides of the boundary.

9. **Delegator intersection asked only when a set resolved — right.** Matches the middleware's own condition; a caller who resolved nothing reaches the projection only for its masking rules, every one of which already applies.

10. **Consumers — nothing beyond the intended safe side.** `plugin-approvals` serves the snapshot fields in the read projection intersected with the query one, so for an approver in this class a masked field is now dropped (the fail-closed shape that seam chose when it landed, not a new behaviour). `service-analytics` admits a member only when both answers carry its field, so for this class a masked field is refused as a group key, aggregate input, filter or sort key, with the engine's own words. On an unreadable posture the approvals seam reads `[]` as the denial its own docblock names. Both suites ran green per the dev report and the whole-root test gate on the head is the verdict.

11. **Public surface.** No spec file, export, REST route or governed path moves. The one REST door that inherits the narrowing without being touched is the anonymous public-form lookup picker: its context names one set, so on a deployment registering no profile for public forms the visitor is in this class, and because the door sorts and searches by its first declared display field, a picker whose first display field declares a masking rule now answers 403 for that class. Covered by the changeset's mechanism and class (a sort key naming the field is refused; a query that must sort or search on it needs the capability or the rule dropped); not named by door, and the door-specific remedy (reorder the display fields, or register a profile holding the capability) is not in the changeset. Judged in ③ as the F4 residual.

12. **Reach.** The dev measured the class reachable at public doors on real boots, correcting the card's source-read (the result masker did not mask either, because the stand-in carried no rule). The dogfood pin boots the real composition for two doors and asserts the scene first; its file lands in the dogfood package's `isolated` project by glob, so the Dogfood Regression Gate's conclusion is the gate verdict on it.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/20995-zero-set-masking.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `minor`, bang in the title, a **BREAKING** banner, and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Right: the diff narrows a published accept set for one caller class (values served, queries admitted, one published projection's answer) and widens nothing, which is exactly the `no (narrowing)` arm; under the launch-window convention a breaking change ships as `minor`, and the no-major guard ran green. `@objectstack/plugin-security` is published; `@objectstack/dogfood` is private, so the dogfood pin needs no changeset. `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- The PR body's line 2 carries the identical declaration.
- ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. Nothing an author can write is removed, renamed or re-meant; no stored shape, spec key or export moves; `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite. The changeset body carries no migration prescription (its "What to do" paragraph is prose without a FROM → TO shape), so the category's statement-against-statement check holds, and the PR Automation run that carries that gate is green.
- The BREAKING text: states the class (who resolves no set but carries a position, a named set or a user id — the exact complement of the shared predicate), the four refused query positions, the echo refusal, the one moved projection, the unresolved-posture refusal and the remedy. One measured consequence is covered by class but not by door: see ① item 11 and ③.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared by the dev; none found.
- Dev deviations, each answered: (a) no WIP push before the first edit — the order's push-only-after-the-fix rule is stricter and the seat accepted it; (b) one wait located a PID by name rather than by the recorded PID — a process-discipline deviation, reported, nothing killed, no effect on the diff; (c) the ablation wrote the whole pre-fix blob and proved landing by blob hash and marker count rather than with the replace tool — accepted by the seat, and the restore was proven byte-identical.
- Surface amendments beside the claim's named regions, same file: the 2.5a gating edit (judged load-bearing in ① item 4) and the byte-for-byte extraction of the principal-less predicate (① item 8). Both declared, both accepted, both right.
- **F4, judged here as the seat asked:** the changeset's BREAKING text covers the public-picker consequence by mechanism and class but does not name the door or its own remedy. Not a defect of the fix (the 403 is the safe side triage directed) and not a gate failure; it is a changelog-completeness residual for the F4 card the seat committed to file. That card should carry the authoring-side question (whether a picker whose first display field declares a masking rule is a shape authoring should refuse) and the two remedies by class. Escalated to the `domain:services` seat for filing.
- **F1, F2, F3:** outside this card's surface, measured, reported by class; the seat committed to file each under the disclosure discipline. F3 is the one that touches this PR's own boundary: the capability fold is deliberately not carried into the stand-in because narrowing `getReadableFields` for this class would move an answer the spec contract states, so it is a `domain:spec` decision. Escalated as the seat recorded.
- **The spec contract docblock** (`getMetadataReadableFields` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) still says the middleware skips its whole field gate for a caller with no permission sets. After this PR that holds for the grant-based gates and not for masking; the answers it states are unchanged. The dev left the spec file alone per the claim and reported it; escalated to the `domain:spec` seat.
- Docs Drift Check (advisory): four hand-written pages name `SecurityPlugin`; the field-level-security page states no zero-set behaviour, so nothing on it is falsified by this diff.
- Triage asked for a re-grade against the measured reach; the seat's ACCEPT carries that request. Not a dev flag; noted for the record.
